content: The prevalence of delusional disorders is estimated to be approximately 24 to 30 cases per 100,000 individuals annually. Delusional disorder accounts for about 1-2% of admissions to inpatient mental health facilities. However, due to the fact that most individuals with delusional disorder do not perceive their condition as an illness or seek treatment, the true prevalence of the disorder is likely underestimated. Delusional disorders are relatively uncommon in psychiatric practice. This rarity may also be underestimated because individuals with the disorder often lack insight into their condition and therefore avoid psychiatric evaluation. The prevalence of delusional disorders is approximately 24 to 30 cases per 100,000 individuals annually. Females are more frequently affected by delusional disorder compared to males. Delusional disorder typically manifests in individuals during middle to late adulthood. The first hospital admissions for delusional disorder generally occur between the ages of 33 and 55 years.
